standard_prerequisites.name: Two closed subsets with empty intersection are defined by ideals generating the unit ideal, and vanishing of a function on a closed set means a power lies in the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology}, cited at proof lines 1950-1951 and 1954-1956
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the unit ideal decomposition and the power statement.

core_obligations: Let the closure of the image be defined by an ideal and use disjointness to conclude that the two ideals generate the unit ideal (proof lines 1948-1951).
Write one as the sum of an element of the source ideal and an element of that ideal (proof lines 1951-1952).
Show the image of the second element vanishes on the closed set of the target ideal, hence a power lies in that ideal (proof lines 1953-1956).
Replace the element by its power to satisfy both requirements (proof lines 1956-1957).
proof_roadmap: Disjointness gives the unit ideal (proof lines 1948-1951).
A power lies in the target ideal (proof lines 1953-1957).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces an element which is congruent to one modulo an ideal of the source and whose image lies in a prescribed ideal of the target, under the hypothesis that the closure of the image of the closed set defined by that ideal is disjoint from the closed set defined by the source ideal. The proof names the ideal defining the closure of the image, uses disjointness of the two closed sets to see that the two ideals generate the unit ideal, writes the resulting decomposition of one, and then uses that the image of the first summand vanishes nowhere on the closed set defined by the target ideal, so that a power of that image lies in the target ideal; replacing the element by that power gives both required properties.
